newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-SINGSPIEL WINS INTERNATIONAL STAKES.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SINGSPIEL WINS INTERNATIONAL STAKES.

text.p: Japan and World Cup winner Singspiel lifted another major title on Tuesday, winning the International Stakes which carried a first prize of $330,000.
Jockey Frankie Dettori sent Singspiel into the lead with three furlongs (600 metres) to go and held on readily by one and a half lengths from Irish Derby winner Desert King, the mount of Mick Kinane.

Third place a length and a half further back was Epsom Derby winner Benny The Dip, ridden by Willie Ryan with Europe's top filly Bosra Sham, partnered by Pat Eddery trailing in a disappointing fourth and last.
Bosra Sham had been sent off at 4-5 favourite but flopped for the second race in succession.

Singspiel had finished only fourth last time out in a big race at Ascot and was allowed by backers to start on Tuesday at the remarkably generous price of 4-1. The five-year-old colt bounced back to his very best form and will now head for the Breeders' Cup later in the year, having run his final race in Europe.
Winning trainer Michael Stoute said: "He was always travelling so well. We didn't have an anxious moment. It was a superbly professional display."
A delighted Dettori, who produced his usual flying dismount in the paddock after another big race victory declared: "He's the best I've ever ridden."
A disappointed Henry Cecil, trainer of Bosra Sham, said: "She lost a shoe. I just hope that's the reason."

Cecil, who replaced Bosra Sham's stable jockey Kieren Fallon after their defeat in the Eclipse Stakes at Sandown Park last month, stuck by his earlier assertion that the filly was the best he had ever trained.
"That wasn't her," he said. "I'm sure there will be another day."

Benny The Dip, the 9-2 third favourite, made all the early running but had nothing left to offer when Singspiel took command and it was Irish raider Desert King (6-1) who produced the strongest challenge in the final 200 metres without ever really threatening the winner.
